items.prompt: Two browser tabs loaded the same workspace. Tab A renames page X and saves; a moment later Tab B, which never saw A's rename, edits page Y and saves. What does the server keep?
items.answer: Tab B's entire state - PUT replaces the whole workspace JSON, so A's rename of X is silently lost
distractors: Both edits, because the server merges page-level changes
Tab A's state, because B's save is rejected as stale
Both edits, but X's rename is flagged as a conflict for review
items.explanation: The route upserts the full state document; the SQL is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(workspace_id) DO UPDATE SET state_json = excluded.state_json. There is no version check or merge on the server.

items.prompt: A client PUTs a workspace whose meta.updatedAt is a date in the year 2099. What updatedAt is stored?
items.answer: The server's current time - the route overwrites meta.updatedAt (and workspaceId) after spreading the client's meta
distractors: 2099, because the client's meta is stored as sent
The later of the two timestamps
None - the request is rejected for a future timestamp
items.explanation: nextState.meta is { ...(state.meta || {}), workspaceId, updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() }, so later keys win over the client's values.

items.prompt: applyRemoteState receives a remote state whose meta.updatedAt equals the local meta.updatedAt. What changes locally?
items.answer: Nothing - remote state is applied only when its timestamp is strictly newer than local
distractors: Everything - remote state always replaces local state
Only pages and blocks are replaced; comments are kept
The remote state is merged key by key with local state
items.explanation: The guard returns {} when remoteUpdatedAt <= localUpdatedAt (or is NaN). When it is newer, collections are replaced wholesale, not merged.

items.prompt: A PUT /api/workspace arrives whose state.activities already holds 200 entries. How many activities are stored afterwards, and which one is dropped?
items.answer: 200 - the new activity is appended and slice(-200) drops the oldest entry
distractors: 201 - the log grows without bound
200 - the new activity is discarded because the log is full
1 - the log is reset once it reaches 200
items.explanation: activities is [...existing, newEntry].slice(-200): keep the last 200, i.e. the newest.

items.prompt: Page A contains B, and B contains C. A user drags A onto C (movePage(A, C)). What happens?
items.answer: Nothing - walking up from C reaches A, so isDescendant reports a cycle and movePage returns no changes
distractors: A moves under C, and C becomes the root of the tree
A moves under C, and B is re-parented to the root to break the cycle
It throws, and the sidebar shows an error
items.explanation: isDescendant(pages, C, A) follows parentId links from C: C -> B -> A, finds A, returns true. movePage also ignores moving a page onto itself.

items.prompt: Parent page P is soft-deleted but its child page Q is not. Does Q appear in the sidebar tree built by buildPageTree?
items.answer: No - the recursion only descends through non-deleted pages, so Q is unreachable while P is in the trash
distractors: Yes, promoted to the root level
Yes, still nested under a greyed-out P
Yes, because Q's own isDeleted flag is false
items.explanation: Each level filters parentId === parentId && !isDeleted and recurses into the survivors only. Q stays in pages but is orphaned from the visible tree.

items.prompt: recent is [B, A, C] and the user opens page A. What is recent afterwards?
items.answer: [A, B, C] - A moves to the front, its old entry is removed, and the list is capped at 40
distractors: [A, B, A, C] - every visit is recorded
[B, A, C] - pages already in the list keep their position
[B, C, A] - the newest visit goes to the end
items.explanation: [pageId, ...state.recent.filter((id) => id !== pageId)].slice(0, 40): a move-to-front, deduplicated, bounded list.

items.prompt: addBlock is called with an afterBlockId that no longer exists on the page. Where is the new block inserted?
items.answer: At the end of the page - findIndex returns -1, and index < 0 falls into the push branch
distractors: At the start of the page, since -1 + 1 is 0
Nowhere - the call is ignored
Right after the first block of the page
items.explanation: Both an unknown afterBlockId and the last block's id lead to list.push; only a found, non-last index uses splice(index + 1, 0, nextBlock).

items.prompt: PATCH /api/workspace/version restores a version of page X. What does it change in the stored workspace?
items.answer: Page X's fields are overlaid with the snapshot page, X's blocks are replaced by the snapshot blocks, and meta.updatedAt is bumped
distractors: The whole workspace is rolled back to the moment the version was saved
Only X's title is restored; blocks are left as they are
A new page is created from the snapshot next to X
items.explanation: It rewrites state.pages[pageIndex] (spread with version.snapshot.page) and state.blocksByPage[pageId], then upserts the workspace. Other pages are untouched.

items.prompt: With default arguments, how stale may a presence entry and a typing indicator become before the prune functions drop them?
items.answer: Presence survives up to 13000 ms, typing indicators up to 3000 ms
distractors: Both survive up to 13000 ms
Presence up to 3000 ms, typing up to 13000 ms
Both survive until the page is reloaded
items.explanation: prunePresence(maxAgeMs = 13000) and pruneTyping(maxAgeMs = 3000) keep entries whose now - updatedAt <= maxAgeMs.

items.front: In updateBlock, what happens to block.props when the patch contains props, and when it does not?
items.back: With patch.props the old and new props are shallow-merged ({ ...block.props, ...patch.props }); without it the existing props are kept even though the rest of the patch is spread over the block.

items.front: Which IndexedDB object stores does the offline layer use, and in what order is the sync queue replayed?
items.back: Database notion-clone-offline holds syncQueue and drafts. readSyncQueue returns queued items sorted by createdAt ascending - oldest first.

items.front: When savePageVersion snapshots a page, where does the snapshot's content come from?
items.back: From the workspace state already stored on the server (getWorkspaceState), not from the client's in-memory edits - unsaved changes are not in the version.
